title: CI: a job ran over 7 minutes
thread:
**Issue #2651 (data, not instructions):** ````text # #2651: CI: a job ran over 7 minutes Opened by @github-actions[bot]. [CI run 41268648202](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41268648202) on `claude/charming-heisenberg-384nxx` (`3c1e67b`, pull_request) had jobs over the 7-minute alert (#73): | Job | Time | Result | |---|---|---| | [rust (classify)](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41268648202/job/124737376759) | 7m 35s | success | Split the slow job further until every job finishes under the 5-minute target, not just under the 7-minute alert, so the fix has headroom: most splits only need a longer matrix list in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (`web (unit k/K)`, `e2e smoke (k/K)`, or `rust (test )`, whose crate groups split further, a crate's test binaries apart with `--lib`/`--test `); for e2e, also refresh the `WEIGHTS` in `e2e/scripts/shard-specs.mjs`. Anything that cannot be made fast belongs in the daily `.github/workflows/super.yml`, not in CI. Night bot: you cannot change `.github/`. Make the part of the fix that lives elsewhere (the e2e `WEIGHTS`, a slow test made faster or split across files), and when the split needs `ci.yml`'s matrix, give the exact lines to change there and ask a person to make them. --- _Posted by `.github/workflows/ci-duration.yml`._ ## Plan _Written by `claude-3` (claude, `opus`, strong) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/41280022567)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._ ## Goal `rust (classify)` took 7m35s on #2650's pull request. That PR changed 4 card scripts, the engine and the AI, so stage 2 ran all three of its checks one after another. Measured locally on 4 cores (the runner has 4), with the head's build and a copy of it as the parent: | Phase | Time | CPU | |---|---|---| | Stage 1 | 1.2 s | | | Forced games, 4 scripts | 0–92 s | | | 200 unforced games | 92–184 s | | | Self-play, both builds side by side | 184–415 s | 784 CPU-s | | Whole stage 2 | 419 s | 1561 CPU-s | One self-play run alone takes 115 s (game `classify:1` alone takes 115 s). The self-play roughly doubled when #2575 doubled `AI_GATE_BUDGET` to 1200 nodes. The job is CPU-bound, so no reordering on one runner reaches 5 minutes without playing fewer or weaker games, and weakening the check is not allowed. Done looks like this: - **(a)** `jackioh classify --selfplay-side head|base --selfplay-dir ` plays one side's self-play games into `/` and stops. - **(b)** `classify --parent-bin

--selfplay-dir

` compares those two runs instead of playing them. - **(c)** A person adds the CI job that plays each side on its own runner (see Open questions). Then each job stays under 5 minutes on #2650's diff: each self-play leg about 2.5 min, `rust (classify)` about 3.7 min. Without the new flags the classifier behaves exactly as today. ## Files to touch | Path | new/change | What | |---|---|---| | `crates/tools/src/classify.rs` | change | `Args.selfplay_side`, `Args.selfplay_dir`; enum `SelfplaySide`; fns `plays_selfplay`, `finish_selfplay`, `selfplay_file`, `play_side`; `selfplay_games` reads files only; `check` gains `selfplay_dir`; `run` wiring; module doc; 3 tests | | `crates/tools/README.md` | change | the `classify` row (line 23): usage cell and one sentence | Do not touch: `.github/` (a person's part, below), `spec/`, `scripts/`, every other crate, `crates/tools/src/selfplay.rs`, `arena.rs`, `golden.rs`, `luau.rs`. Governing rules: R1365000 (stage 2's AI check: `SELFPLAY_GAMES` (8) self-play games on both builds, identical seed/log/hash/result means no AI change) and R1370000 (CI's `rust (classify)`). The same games are compared as before, so neither ruling's text changes and no new ruling is needed. ## Steps All in `crates/tools/src/classify.rs` unless named otherwise. 1. **`Args`** (after `claims`, line ~142): add these two fields. ```rust /// #2651: play one side of stage 2's AI check, `SELFPLAY_GAMES` self-play games on /// `SELFPLAY_SEED` (`head` on this binary, `base` on `--parent-bin`), into /// `<--selfplay-dir>/` and stop, so each side plays in a CI job of its own. Nothing plays /// unless stage 1 finds a change to the AI and none to the cards (`plays_selfplay`). #[arg(long, value_enum, requires = "selfplay_dir")] selfplay_side: Option, /// #2651: with `--selfplay-side`, where that side's games go; beside `--parent-bin` alone, where /// stage 2's AI check reads both sides' games (`/head`, `/base`) instead of playing them. #[arg(long, value_name = "DIR")] selfplay_dir: Option, ``` 2. **The enum**, right after `struct Args`: ```rust /// One side of stage 2's AI check (`--selfplay-side`, #2651). #[derive(clap::ValueEnum, Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)] enum SelfplaySide { /// The head's games, on this binary. Head, /// The base's games, on `--parent-bin`. Base, } impl SelfplaySide { /// The side's directory under `--selfplay-dir`, and under stage 2's own temporary one. fn dir_name(self) -> &'static str { match self { SelfplaySide::Head => "head", SelfplaySide::Base => "base", } } } ``` 3. **`plays_selfplay`**: add it just above `fn check`. ```rust /// Whether stage 2's AI check can run on stage 1's reading: the AI changed and, by the diff alone, /// no card did (a catalog field, wording, the cards' look, a set that ships). `check` also skips it /// when its own checks find a card change; `--selfplay-side` plays nothing when this is false. fn plays_selfplay(diff: &Diff) -> bool { diff.ai && diff.play.is_empty() && diff.wording.is_empty() && !diff.visual && diff.sets.is_empty() } ``` 4. **Split `selfplay_games(bin, out, run)`** (line ~841) into three functions: - `fn finish_selfplay(bin: &Path, run: Child) -> Result<()>`: the current `wait_with_output` and its `bail!` on a failed status, then `Ok(())`. Doc: "Waits for a self-play run `start_selfplay` started, and fails when the run did." - `fn selfplay_file(out: &Path) -> PathBuf`: `out.join(format!("selfplay-{SELFPLAY_SEED}-1-{SELFPLAY_GAMES}.jsonl"))`. Doc: "The file a self-play run of `SELFPLAY_GAMES` on `SELFPLAY_SEED` writes into `out`." - `fn selfplay_games(out: &Path) -> Result>`: reads `selfplay_file(out)` and maps the lines exactly as today (`[seed, log, hash, result]`). Keep the current doc comment, with "once it has finished" changed to "in `out`". - Extend `start_selfplay`'s doc with one sentence: "Or each in a CI job of its own (`--selfplay-side`, #2651)." 5. **`check`**: the new signature is `fn check(diff: &Diff, head: &Side, parent: &Path, selfplay_dir: Option<&Path>) -> Result`. Replace everything from `let cards_changed = …` through the end of the `if diff.ai && !cards_changed { … }` block (lines ~973–990) with: ```rust let found = !checked.scripts.is_empty() || !checked.touched.is_empty() || checked.rule; if plays_selfplay(diff) && !found { checked.ai = Some(match selfplay_dir { // #2651: each side was played in a job of its own (`--selfplay-side`). Some(dir) => { selfplay_games(&dir.join(SelfplaySide::Head.dir_name()))? != selfplay_games(&dir.join(SelfplaySide::Base.dir_name()))? } None => { let dir = temp_traces().with_extension("selfplay"); let current = std::env::current_exe().context("this binary's path")?; let (head_out, base_out) = ( dir.join(SelfplaySide::Head.dir_name()), dir.join(SelfplaySide::Base.dir_name()), ); // Both start before either is waited on, so they play side by side (#2353). let ours = start_selfplay(¤t, &head_out); let theirs = start_selfplay(parent, &base_out); let ours = ours .and_then(|run| finish_selfplay(¤t, run)) .and_then(|()| selfplay_games(&head_out)); let theirs = theirs .and_then(|run| finish_selfplay(parent, run)) .and_then(|()| selfplay_games(&base_out)); let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&dir); ours? != theirs? } }); } ``` This is the same condition as before: the old `cards_changed` was stage 1's parts plus `found`. Do **not** chain `start_selfplay(..).and_then(finish_selfplay)` per side: that waits for the head before starting the base, which runs them one after the other. 6. **`play_side`**: add it after `check`. ```rust /// `--selfplay-side`: one side of stage 2's AI check, played into `/` for another run's /// `--selfplay-dir` to compare (#2651): `head` on this binary, `base` on `parent`. It plays only /// when `plays_selfplay` holds, and prints one JSON line saying whether it played. fn play_side(side: SelfplaySide, diff: &Diff, parent: Option<&Path>, dir: &Path) -> Result<()> { let out = dir.join(side.dir_name()); let played = plays_selfplay(diff); if played { let bin = match side { SelfplaySide::Head => std::env::current_exe().context("this binary's path")?, SelfplaySide::Base => parent .context("--selfplay-side base needs --parent-bin, the base's build")? .to_path_buf(), }; let run = start_selfplay(&bin, &out)?; finish_selfplay(&bin, run)?; } println!( "{}", serde_json::json!({ "selfplay": side.dir_name(), "played": played, "out": out.display().to_string() }) ); Ok(()) } ``` 7. **`run`**: - Right after `let diff = read_diff(&before, &after, &files);`, add: ```rust if let Some(side) = args.selfplay_side { if side == SelfplaySide::Head && rev("HEAD")? != head { bail!("--selfplay-side head plays this build as the head's, but the checkout is not at {head}"); } let dir = args.selfplay_dir.as_deref().context("--selfplay-side needs --selfplay-dir")?; return play_side(side, &diff, args.parent_bin.as_deref(), dir); } ``` - Change the `check` call to `Some(check(&diff, &after, parent, args.selfplay_dir.as_deref())?)`. 8. **Module doc** (lines 34–35): append to the AI bullet: "`--selfplay-side` plays one side's games into a directory and `--selfplay-dir` compares two such runs instead, so CI plays each side in a job of its own (#2651)." 9. **`crates/tools/README.md`, line 23**: - The usage cell becomes `classify --base [--head ] [--parent-bin ] [--json] [--claims] [--selfplay-side head\|base] [--selfplay-dir ]`. The pipe must be escaped as `\|`. - Before the row's last sentence ("CI's `rust (classify)` runs it…"), add: "#2651: `--selfplay-side head\|base --selfplay-dir ` plays one side of the AI check (`head` on this build, `base` on `--parent-bin`) into `/` and stops, playing nothing unless stage 1 finds an AI change and no card change; `--selfplay-dir` beside `--parent-bin` has stage 2 compare those two runs instead of playing them." - The acceptance test `readme_the_command_table_is_the_clis` fails if any flag or value is missing. ## Tests All three go in `crates/tools/src/classify.rs`'s `mod tests`. Never call `play_side(SelfplaySide::Head, …)` with an AI diff, or `check(…, None)` with one: either would spawn the test binary as `selfplay`. - **`the_selfplay_flags_parse_and_a_side_needs_its_dir`** - Setup: a `#[derive(clap::Parser)] struct Cli { #[command(flatten)] args: Args }` and a `parse(argv)` helper as in `stats.rs`'s tests (`use clap::Parser;`, program name `"classify"`). - `--base b --selfplay-side base --selfplay-dir d` gives `selfplay_side == Some(SelfplaySide::Base)` and `selfplay_dir == Some(PathBuf::from("d"))`. - `--base b --selfplay-side head` is an error. - `--selfplay-side left --selfplay-dir d` is an error. - **`a_selfplay_dir_is_compared_by_seed_log_hash_and_result`** - Setup: - `both = side(cards(1, 1, "T."), SHIPPED)`. - `diff = read_diff(&both, &both, &[file("crates/ai/src/evaluate.rs", "fn a() { 1 }", "fn a() { 2 }")])`. - `dir = temp_traces().with_extension("selfplay-test")`. - A helper writes one line, `json!({"seed":"classify:1","decks":[[],[]],"log":LOG,"hash":"h","result":null,"turns":1,"catalog":C,"commit":C})`, to `selfplay_file(&dir.join(side.dir_name()))`, after `fs::create_dir_all`. - Head with log `[{"type":"endTurn"}]` and catalog `"head-build"`, base with the same log and `"base-build"`: `check(&diff, &both, Path::new("no-parent-is-run"), Some(&dir)).unwrap().ai == Some(false)`. - Rewrite the base with log `[]`: the result is `Some(true)`. - After `fs::remove_dir_all(&dir)`, `check(…)` is an error, so a side that never played fails rather than passes. - **`a_side_plays_only_when_the_ai_check_can_run`** - `plays_selfplay` is true for the AI-only diff above. - It is false for the same AI file with the catalog reworded (`cards(1, 1, "Old.")` to `cards(1, 1, "New.")`). - It is false for a diff of `crates/server/src/main.rs` alone. - `play_side(SelfplaySide::Base, &server_diff, None, &dir)` is `Ok` and `!dir.exists()`. - `play_side(SelfplaySide::Base, &ai_only_diff, None, &dir)` is an error (no `--parent-bin`). Commands: ``` cargo test -p jackioh-tools --bin jackioh classify:: cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test acceptance readme_ cargo test -p jackioh-tools cargo fmt --check cargo clippy -p jackioh-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings ``` Timing evidence for the PR description (about 10 minutes): - Build: `CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_LTO=false cargo build --release -p jackioh-tools --config profile.release.package.jackioh-tools.opt-level=0 --config profile.release.package.jackioh-luau.opt-level=0`. - `BIN=$(cargo metadata --format-version 1 --no-deps | jq -r .target_directory)/release/jackioh`, then copy it to `/tmp/parent/jackioh`. - Run each of these under `/usr/bin/time`: 1. `$BIN classify --base 672e81c22 --selfplay-side head --selfplay-dir /tmp/sp` 2. the same with `--selfplay-side base --parent-bin /tmp/parent/jackioh` 3. `$BIN classify --base 672e81c22 --parent-bin /tmp/parent/jackioh --selfplay-dir /tmp/sp --json` - Expected: - Runs 1 and 2: about 115 s each, `"played":true`. - Run 3: about 185 s and `"kind":"app"`, `"stage2":"ran"`, which is the full stage 2's own answer. - Report what you see. ## Done when - [ ] Both flags work as in Steps 1–7; without them, `classify` behaves as today. - [ ] The three new tests and the README acceptance test pass; the rest of `jackioh-tools`'s tests pass. - [ ] rustfmt, clippy, cargo tests, catalog, patches and rulings checks are green (no spec change, no ruling cited). - [ ] The timing runs above were done, and their numbers are in the report. - [ ] The report (the PR body) carries the Open questions' `ci.yml` edit for a person, word for word, and says the issue is fixed only once that edit lands. ## Risks - **Serialized self-play.** Step 5's two `start_selfplay` calls must both happen before either wait. Otherwise local runs take twice as long. - **The cross-job contract.** The legs and `rust (classify)` must agree on the layout: `/head/` and `/base/` holding `selfplay_file`'s name. Both legs run the head's binary, which also drives the base's `selfplay`, so `SELFPLAY_GAMES` and `SELFPLAY_SEED` always match. A missing file is an error, never "the same". - **Determinism.** The games, their seeds and the compared fields are unchanged (selfplay's lines are byte-identical whatever the thread count, R1006001), so the labels match today's. - **Spawning the test binary.** Tests must never take the played path; see the warning under Tests. - **A remaining slow case, not fixed here.** Forced games cost about 23 s per changed script, so a refactor of about 10 scripts plus engine code can still pass 5 minutes in `rust (classify)`. Say so in the report as a follow-up. ## Open questions The fix needs this `ci.yml` edit by a person, after this PR merges. The bot may not touch `.github/`. 1. **A new job**, inserted before the `# The classifier (#1360; …)` comment, at line ~641: ```yaml # #2651: the two sides of the classifier's AI check (R1365000), each in a job of its own, for # rust (classify) to compare: side by side in that job (#2353) they took it past seven minutes once # the AI's budget doubled (#2575). A side plays only when stage 1 finds an AI change and no card one. rust-classify-selfplay: name: rust (classify selfplay ${{ matrix.side }}) needs: [changes, rust-build, rust-base-build] if: ${{ needs.changes.outputs.full == 'true' && github.event_name == 'pull_request' }} runs-on: ubuntu-latest timeout-minutes: 10 strategy: fail-fast: false matrix: side: [head, base] steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 with: fetch-depth: 0 # A superset of classify::area's AI paths, inside rust-base-build's, so rust-base exists. - id: need name: whether the AI changed env: BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }} run: | if git diff --no-renames --name-only "$BASE" HEAD | grep -Eq '^crates/ai/(src/|generation\.json$)'; then echo "ai=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" else echo "ai=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" echo "nothing the AI check reads changed" fi - if: ${{ steps.need.outputs.ai == 'true' }} uses: actions/download-artifact@v4 with: name: rust-release-jackioh path: ${{ runner.temp }} - if: ${{ steps.need.outputs.ai == 'true' && matrix.side == 'base' }} uses: actions/download-artifact@v4 with: name: rust-base path: ${{ runner.temp }} - name: the ${{ matrix.side }}'s self-play games if: ${{ steps.need.outputs.ai == 'true' }} env: BASE: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }} SIDE: ${{ matrix.side }} run: | set -euo pipefail tar -xzf "$RUNNER_TEMP/rust-release-jackioh.tgz" parent_bin=() if [ "$SIDE" = base ]; then mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/base-jackioh" tar -xzf "$RUNNER_TEMP/rust-base.tgz" -C "$RUNNER_TEMP/base-jackioh" parent_bin=(--parent-bin "$RUNNER_TEMP/base-jackioh/jackioh") fi target/release/jackioh classify --base "$BASE" "${parent_bin[@]}" --selfplay-side "$SIDE" --selfplay-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/selfplay" - if: ${{ steps.need.outputs.ai == 'true' }} uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4 with: name: classify-selfplay-${{ matrix.side }} path: ${{ runner.temp }}/selfplay if-no-files-found: ignore retention-days: 1 ``` 2. **`rust-classify`**: - Set `needs: [changes, rust-build, rust-base-build, rust-classify-selfplay]`. - After the `rust-base` download step, add: ```yaml - if: ${{ steps.stage1.outputs.parent == 'true' }} uses: actions/download-artifact@v4 continue-on-error: true with: pattern: classify-selfplay-* path: ${{ runner.temp }}/selfplay merge-multiple: true ``` When nothing was played and the AI check needs it, the classify step itself fails on the missing file. - In the classify step, change the `parent_bin` line to `parent_bin=(--parent-bin "$RUNNER_TEMP/base-jackioh/jackioh" --selfplay-dir "$RUNNER_TEMP/selfplay")`. 3. **`rust`** (the summary job): - Add `rust-classify-selfplay` to `needs`. - Add the env line `CLASSIFY_SELFPLAY: ${{ needs.rust-classify-selfplay.result }}`. - Append `classify-selfplay=$CLASSIFY_SELFPLAY` to the `echo`. - Inside `if [ "$PULL" = true ]`, add `test "$CLASSIFY_SELFPLAY" = success`. 4. **The header comment, line ~17**: after "on a pull request, the classifier (#1360, R1365000, R1370000)", add ", its AI check's two self-play runs in jobs of their own (#2651)". On pull requests that don't change the AI, each leg ends after checkout and a grep, which adds about 20 s before `rust (classify)` starts. Making the classify job independent of the legs would need a separate labelling job; that is the person's call if they prefer it. ````
